soundness_flags.label: ass:binary-fixed-potential-outcomes
soundness_flags.one_line: Neyman1923 supports a finite-population potential-yield/randomization model but not the stated binary-support restriction, so this standard tag needs a binary-outcome source or a corrected name/citation.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: honest_scope / all statements indexed by s or (s_J)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Armwise pair discordance is latent and s is an analyst-selected sensitivity value, not a quantity verified from pretreatment data.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All risk, optimizer, asymptotic, and coverage claims are conditional on the selected s or sequence (s_J); no data-driven validation or selection of that sensitivity bound is claimed.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The translated paper introduces a doubly indexed array of unknown potential crop yields and an urn randomization model; it does not impose binary potential outcomes.

source_verification_receipts.version: Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences, 2015
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The text distinguishes randomized assignment mechanisms from outcome-dependent observational assignment and supports treating the assignment law as fixed independently of potential outcomes in a randomized experiment.
Theorem 2.1 applies to a given assignment vector and invariant estimator under group invariance; the subsequent section separately studies optimal linear estimation schemes under further assumptions.
The paper studies minimax precision over conditional-mean classes, allows mixed-strategy designs, and frames inference-constrained mixed-strategy design separately from the precision criterion.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1--2, Introduction and main-results display; pp. 21--23, proofs of Theorems 2.2--2.3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For unrestricted binary potential-outcome schedules the paper reduces the problem to a binomial experiment, identifies balanced Bernoulli assignment with a nonlinear shrinkage rule, and states the Airy second-order expansion.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 3, discussion of Proposition 1 and Theorem 1; pp. 7--9, Theorem 1 and its discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 optimizes over all measurable estimators for unrestricted bounded potential outcomes; the paper identifies independent random assignment and reduces the bounded box through endpoint arguments.
Among stratified schemes treating units with probability one half, the paper establishes an optimal matched-pair design, with prognostic/baseline-outcome pairing as a special case.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(548), 2024
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The Gram--Schmidt Walk paper formalizes a balance--robustness tradeoff for Horvitz--Thompson estimation, gives finite-sample MSE control, and supplies asymptotic normality and conservative variance estimation under its conditions.
The paper concerns design-unbiased estimation of a bounded finite-population total and characterizes pairwise-independent inclusion indicators as attaining its sharp worst-case bound.
The paper gives matched-pair binary-outcome randomization inference under within-pair coin flips and identifies a single worst compatible boundary corner.
The paper gives exact binary ATE intervals using O(log n) tests for balanced Bernoulli and matched-pair designs, with a separate general-Bernoulli extension.

The paper develops exact/conservative ATE confidence sets in stratified binary experiments by maximizing permutation p-values over compatible potential-outcome tables and gives product-form computational bounds.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the Neyman1923 tag on binary support with a precise binary finite-population source, or rename the condition as a binary outcome-support restriction and cite one of the exact binary randomization-inference papers.

Add a fully worked exact rational orbit certificate for J=2,s=1, including the displayed noncanonical q, estimator coordinates, and dual prior; this makes the separation independently auditable rather than only reported numerically.

State an explicit finite-dimensional second-order variational problem for a concrete critical path such as s_J=floor(J/2), then use it as the first target of Open-ended Question 6 before quantifying over every local approach.

recommended_next_step: Correct the binary-support assumption citation/tag, retain the accepted conditional sensitivity scope, and then advance this field-tier design-minimax angle to Stage 0.
